issues.translation_quote: You should eat when you drink! Hurry!
issues.justification: Ivan's line is an urgent call for a snack/food; the translation turns it into a vague moralizing proverb that doesn't fit the panicked context.

issues.translation_quote: Score! Score!
issues.justification: The crowd chants the hockey cheer 'Puck, puck!' (a Soviet fan chant); the translation loses the reference and the absurd anachronism joke.

issues.translation_quote: Keep your mouth open!
issues.justification: Shpak the dentist is told not to close his mouth (patient's mouth); the translation is nonsensical without the dental context, and 'keep your mouth open' reads as a command to the wrong person.

issues.translation_quote: Profession de foi!
issues.justification: The pun on 'professional' mispronounced as French by the actor is lost; 'profession de foi' means 'declaration of faith' in English usage and the joke does not land.

issues.source_quote: Я Вам как представитель общественности заявляю: прекратить!
issues.translation_quote: As a representative of the community, I order you to stop!
issues.justification: Minor: but 'Не вели казнить' register aside, this is acceptable; however the title 'Тамбовский волк тебе боярин' is translated as 'I'm no boyar, you loon!', losing the idiom and its humor.

issues.translation_quote: I'm no boyar, you loon!
issues.justification: The idiom 'Tambov wolf is your boyar' (a rude Soviet-era retort) is flattened; the comic rudeness is lost.

issues.source_quote: Это он из роли. Ну, вот роль такая! Эта роль ругательная
issues.translation_quote: He's in character. That's his role! Then it's an insulting role.
issues.justification: Speaker attribution and sense are muddled; the original is a continuous complaint about the abusive role, and the 'Then' adds an unwarranted connective.

issues.translation_quote: Well, sinful beard!
issues.justification: Odd literal rendering of an archaic jocular address; fails to convey the Tsar's mock-regal tone.

issues.source_quote: Не вели казнить, Великий государь, надежа! Демоны тебя схватили!
issues.translation_quote: Have mercy, great sovereign, our hope and protector!
issues.justification: 'Не вели казнить' is a fixed formula of the boyar court ('Do not order me executed'); the translation alters it to a generic 'have mercy', and varied renderings across the text weaken a running joke.

issues.translation_quote: You can't treat interpreters like that!
issues.justification: Acceptable, but preceding 'в кипятке и сварили' rendered as 'boiled him alive' adds 'alive' and loses the deadpan; moderate issue.

issues.source_quote: Дер гроссер кениг, дас шведишен кенигсрейх, зандте мих.
issues.translation_quote: Der grosse König des schwedischen Königreichs sandte mich, seinen treuen Diener, zu Euch, Zar und Grossfürst Iwan Wassiljewitsch von ganz Russland.
issues.justification: The source is deliberately broken, phonetic pseudo-German (Russian-transliterated, ungrammatical, ending in 'Усарусса'); the translation replaces it with fluent correct German, destroying the comic effect and the characters' inability to understand.

issues.translation_quote: Kemsk volost!
issues.justification: Untranslated/unexplained; later 'Kem district' is used, creating inconsistency; the joke of the ambassador's broken Russian is not conveyed.

issues.source_quote: Вы свoими развoдами резкo снижаете наши пoказатели.
issues.translation_quote: Your divorces are seriously hurting our statistics.
issues.justification: Bureaucratic satire is partly kept, but 'Это дело общественное' is rendered 'a matter for the community', which is acceptable; minor loss of Soviet 'показатели' (performance indicators).

issues.source_quote: Не вели казнить, Великий государь, надежа!
issues.translation_quote: Have mercy, great sovereign, our hope!
issues.justification: Inconsistent rendering of the same formula throughout.

issues.translation_quote: You're a strange man!
issues.justification: 'Оригинальный' is sarcastic ('You're quite the character'); 'strange' is flatter.

issues.source_quote: Ох, как это глупо! Из ревности оскорблять человека!
issues.translation_quote: Oh, how childish! Insulting him out of jealousy!
issues.justification: 'Глупо' is 'silly/stupid'; 'childish' shifts the meaning slightly.

issues.source_quote: Ты по что боярыню обидел, смерд?!
issues.translation_quote: Why hast thou wronged the lady, you peasant?!
issues.justification: Mixes 'thou/hast' with 'you', producing an inconsistent register.

issues.translation_quote: Verily, forsooth... I'm most grateful to you!
issues.justification: The joke is the Tsar's archaic Slavonic phrasing alongside Bunsha's mangled attempt; the English pastiche is generic.

issues.translation_quote: Whose man are you?
issues.justification: Fine, but the following 'Whose serf' clarification is inserted as new wording; acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Вот смотрит! Вы на мне дыру протрете.
issues.translation_quote: There he goes again! You'll wear a hole in me.
issues.justification: 'There he goes again' adds a nuance not in the source.

issues.source_quote: Это, стало быть, ты тут живешь?
issues.translation_quote: So this is where you live?
issues.justification: Loses the archaic 'стало быть' flavor of Ivan's speech.
